prologue.title: Prologue · Before qualifying
prologue.summary: Qualify in the Qingyu harbour pool and sheltered water offshore.

ch1.title: Chapter 1 · Harbours and ships
ch1.summary: Fishing pier, freighter hull, and in-harbour search. The chapter sign-off is the Class II pilot exam.

ch2.title: Chapter 2 · Fish farms
ch2.summary: Offshore pen nets: nets, morts, and moorings. Requires a Class II pilot licence.

p0_induction.title: Pool induction
p0_induction.summary: Ma Li flies alongside. Observe depth drift at the north wall, then photograph three plates.
p0_induction.brief: Qingyu training pool. Fresh water, no current. Zhou Kai has the tether and Ma Li is coaching. Photograph the north, east and south wall plates in that order. Lin Cen will check the shots.

radio.speaker: Lin Cen
radio.start: R-One, Tide Control. First watch together. Check in.

p1_pool_checkout.title: Pool checkout dive
p1_pool_checkout.summary: Arm, hover, photograph three pool walls and return to launch. About 15–20 min.
p1_pool_checkout.brief: YX-TR-001 · YX Model R. Complete the pre-dive checklist. Arm the thrusters only after launch. Hover in the centre of the pool for 20 seconds. Take one photo with the instrument overlay on each wall: north, east and south. Return to the launch point for recovery.

radio.speaker: Lin Cen
radio.start: In water. Arm when the platform is clear.
radio.partial: Everyone back safe. Repeat the run.

deliverables.recover: Return to launch, ready for recovery

p2_open_water.title: Open-water trainee exam
p2_open_water.summary: Four buoys, depth hold, and a drift check with sticks released. Real mode, 15–20 min.
p2_open_water.brief: YX-TR-002. In sheltered water outside Qingyu Harbour, pass four checkpoints in order with depth hold engaged. Release the sticks to see how the vehicle drifts in the light current. Steady it, then return to launch. Stick input controls thrust, not speed. Pass in Real mode to earn your trainee pilot licence.

radio.speaker: Lin Cen
radio.start: R-1, four buoy checkpoints, in order.
radio.done: Familiarization complete. Back to the boat.
radio.partial: Right call coming back. Repeat the familiarization dive.

c1_pier_level1.title: First work order outside the dock
c1_pier_level1.summary: Level I inspection. Photograph each of the six jetty piles and keep the tether clear.
c1_pier_level1.brief: The port authority needs a visual survey before typhoon season. No measurements this time. Under the jetty, photograph each of the six piles in rows A and B at about 6 m depth. The pile just needs to be visible. The cross-current runs east. Plan your way back before rounding a pile, and keep the tether clear for recovery. A quay wall overview would be welcome if you have time. Same pay, though.

radio.speaker: Supervisor Lin
radio.start: First outdoor ticket. A-He's on deck watching the line—you watch the piles.
radio.done: Authority says the photos are clear. They've taken whole rolls of mud before.
radio.partial: Hand these in. I'll tell the authority the rest wait for another day.

c1_pier_level2.title: Pier Level II sample: marine growth
c1_pier_level2.summary: Three nominated piles, two elevations each: measure growth thickness with the laser scaler.
c1_pier_level2.brief: Authority reviewed last job's photos and wants to know how thick the growth really is. Level II sample: piles A1, A3, B2 at 4 m and 12 m depth. Close to about 1 m, square to the face, steady—put the laser dots on the growth layer and wait for a stable reading. Then back to launch as usual.

radio.speaker: Supervisor Lin
radio.start: Laser dots on the barnacles—not on the fish.
radio.done: Numbers look clean. Authority wants them against last year—take it as a compliment.
radio.partial: I'll log the missing points; we'll fill them when tide is kinder.

c1_hull_fouling.title: Freighter hull fouling rating
c1_hull_fouling.summary: 80 m freighter: one rating photo each of both bilge keels, propeller, and rudder. Confirm LOTO before the prop.
c1_hull_fouling.brief: Fleet ops need to decide whether to clean the bottom this call. One photo each of port and starboard bilge keels, propeller blades, and rudder for fouling rating. At the prop, confirm main engine stopped and shaft locked out (LOTO) with the ship before you close in—inside three metres without confirmation is a safety fail. Under the hull there's no surface reference; watch your depth and tether.

radio.speaker: A-He
radio.start: The chief says the main engine is stopped. Get his confirmation that the shaft is locked out.
radio.done: Ops says the rating's clear enough; they'll clean next week. You just saved the company money.
radio.partial: Send what you've got. Prop area next time.

c1_dropped_object.title: Lost equipment in harbour
c1_dropped_object.summary: Visibility is less than a metre. Locate the lost survey instrument with sonar, then confirm it on camera.
c1_dropped_object.brief: The survey crew lost an instrument overboard, probably within 20 metres northeast of the launch point. Visibility is less than a metre. Settle on the bottom and sweep with imaging sonar. Read the bearing, turn towards the return and approach slowly. Take a photo once you can identify the instrument. Keep thrust low to avoid stirring up silt.

radio.speaker: Works crew · Old Cai
radio.start: That unit costs more than my car. Please.
radio.done: Found it! Divers hang a line this afternoon. I owe you lunch.
radio.partial: At least we know the area. Thanks.

c1_quay_cp.title: Quay sheet-pile CP spot checks
c1_quay_cp.summary: Side job: three wall points—seat the CP probe and read potential; flag under-protected spots.
c1_quay_cp.brief: Authority trusts us enough for a small add-on: three cathodic protection potential spot checks on the quay wall. Seat the probe gently, hold steady a few seconds for a reading; slamming in doesn't count and costs score. Anything more positive than −800 mV is under-protected—flag it in the report.

radio.speaker: Supervisor Lin
radio.done: Point three is under-protected; they'll schedule anode change-out. Good find.

c1_hull_ut.title: Hull thickness spot checks
c1_hull_ut.summary: Side job: four side-shell UT points for the annual class survey.
c1_hull_ut.brief: The annual class survey needs four thickness readings from the hull plating. On each side, take one forward and one aft of midships, at about 4 m depth. Hold the probe steady against the steel for a reliable reading. Stay clear of the propeller. Under the hull you have no surface reference.

radio.speaker: A-He
radio.start: Four points, then we're done. Deck lunch is pork chop today.
radio.done: All in tolerance. Surveyor will be happy; owner happier.
radio.partial: Surveyor will chase the missing points—hand in what you have.

c1_signoff_exam.title: Chapter end: pre-handover recheck (Class II exam)
c1_signoff_exam.summary: Class II exam: revisit three prior anomalies, re-shoot from the original angles so the next shift can find them. Full realism.
c1_signoff_exam.brief: This port job is your Class II pilot exam. The port authority needs an update on three defects. Crack on pile A2 at 10 m, concrete spall on B3 at 14 m, chip on the south quay wall at 12 m—re-shoot square-on from the original stand-off (about 1–2.5 m); then hold position for a 6-second visual check at the middle of the quay wall. Keep the tether off the piles; finish everything before recovery.

radio.speaker: Supervisor Lin
radio.start: Still me examining. Photos the next shift can read—that's the test.
radio.done: Pass. Class II card ships to the company; next month you can take fish-farm work.
radio.partial: Close. Work the camera angles; retest next week.

deliverables.quay_chip: South quay wall · chip at 12 m
deliverables.quay_station: Mid quay wall · 6 s visual check in position

c2_net_inspection.title: Net inspection
c2_net_inspection.summary: At slack water, circle the outside of the pen. Find and photograph two holes. Keep the netting clear of the thrusters.
c2_net_inspection.brief: Farm manager says fish are disappearing daily—suspects torn net. On slack tide, orbit outside the pen (east, north, west, south all required). Stop square-on for photos of any holes. Don't hug the net—thrusters will suck mesh in; keep your tether clear of mooring lines.

radio.speaker: Farm manager · A-Mei
radio.start: Fish spook easy. Go slow and they won't scatter.
radio.done: Both holes found—we'll patch this afternoon. Thanks.
radio.partial: Patch what you found; check the rest next slack tide.

c2_mort_recovery.title: Mort recovery (Model V)
c2_mort_recovery.summary: Launch Model V from the pen walkway. Use its manipulator to lift dead fish from the net floor, one at a time.
c2_mort_recovery.brief: A few morts on the net floor will foul water quality if left. Launch straight into the pen from the walkway. Only Model V has a manipulator, so it goes. Descend to the floor, grip morts one by one and lift clear; trim shifts once you clamp—take it slow. Hitting the floor spooks the whole pen.

radio.speaker: Farm manager · A-Mei
radio.done: Floor looks cleaner. Next time, dinner—live fish.
radio.partial: Take these; we'll net the rest.

deliverables.first_fish: Grip one mort and lift clear of the floor
deliverables.recover: Return to in-pen launch for recovery

c2_mooring_exam.title: Chapter end: post-typhoon ground lines (pen endorsement exam)
c2_mooring_exam.summary: Follow the two southern ground lines from buoy to anchor; record line condition. Full realism.
c2_mooring_exam.brief: Typhoon just passed; manager needs to know the mooring still holds. Drop at the southeast and southwest corner buoys, follow each ground line to the anchor, and shoot a condition photo mid-line. Keep your tether clear of the ground lines. This is the pen-ops endorsement exam.

radio.speaker: Supervisor Lin
radio.start: Swell will bounce you up and down—that's normal, not you.
radio.done: Endorsement's in. Farms will ask for you by name now.
radio.partial: Almost. Retest on the next slack tide.

none.label: Cadet (unlicensed)
none.opens: In-house training and pool checkout dives

trainee.label: Trainee pilot
trainee.opens: Simple in-harbour jobs: pier Level I, hull, harbour search

grade2.label: Class II pilot
grade2.opens: Detailed pier and hull work, fish farms

senior.label: Senior pilot
senior.opens: Subsea cable, night ops, multi-vehicle (later chapters)

supervisor.label: Supervisor
supervisor.opens: Watch and direct operational jobs (later chapters)

laser_scaler.label: Laser scaler
laser_scaler.use: Two parallel laser dots on the target put a known spacing in the image so you can measure size.
laser_scaler.unlocks: Growth thickness, defect size, and other measured deliverables (Level II jobs)

imaging_sonar.label: Imaging sonar
imaging_sonar.use: When visibility fails, image with sound to find targets and structure, then confirm by camera.
imaging_sonar.unlocks: In-harbour dropped-object and other search jobs

cp_probe.label: Cathodic protection (CP) probe
cp_probe.use: Seat the probe on steel and read potential vs the reference electrode to judge protection.
cp_probe.unlocks: CP survey deliverables on sheet pile and steelwork

ut_gauge.label: Ultrasonic thickness gauge (UT)
ut_gauge.use: Seat the probe on plate to measure remaining wall thickness and find corrosion thinning.

gripper.label: Work gripper kit
gripper.use: Work gripper and catch basket for the YX Model V manipulator—standard kit for recovery jobs.
gripper.unlocks: Mort, dropped-object, and other recovery jobs

sticker_yx_logo.label: YX company logo sticker
sticker_yx_logo.use: YX marks on both sides of the vehicle. Clients on deck know whose bird it is at a glance.

sticker_yx_stripe.label: YX orange-white livery stripe
sticker_yx_stripe.use: Company fleet orange-white diagonal stripe—easier to spot in murky water.
